span.term: rTMS spreads transsynaptically into two networks whose interaction is nonlinear, so perturbing ventral PPC dissociates attention from consciousness instead of moving them together
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: a focal coil at near-threshold intensity limits the induced neural interference within a widely distributed network, which is why the behavioural effect is only about 10%
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: the stimulation disrupts the spatial disengagement operation of Posner's attention system, which then lengthens reaction time
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The behavioural effect of the stimulation was small, attributed to the focal coil and near-threshold intensity used.
span.note: what this limits: the SIZE of the reported effect: THE SMALL BUT SIGNIFICANT MAGNITUDE OF rTMS EFFECTS ON VENTRAL PPC (ABOUT 10%) IS LIKELY DUE TO THE USE OF FOCAL COIL AND NEAR-THRESHOLD INTENSITY OF rTMS
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: rTMS effects are not confined to the targeted region, so the locus of the effect is not purely ventral PPC.
span.note: what this limits: any claim that localises the effect to ventral PPC: THE EFFECT OF rTMS DOES NOT REMAIN LIMITED TO THE TARGETED BRAIN REGION BUT SPREAD TRANSYNAPTICALLY
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: A motor-output contribution to the reaction-time slowing cannot be excluded.
span.note: what this limits: the reaction-time interpretation: THE SLOWING OF THE REACTION TIME IS MAINLY DUE TO VISUOSPATIAL SENSORY PROCESSING, ALTHOUGH A SLIGHT INFLUENCE ON MOTOR OUTPUT CANNOT BE EXCLUDED
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The paper's consciousness measure is the percentage of trials a subject reported seeing.
span.note: what this limits: any citation of this paper as evidence about consciousness: trials associated with the conscious perception of the cue stimuli were defined as seen trials, and the reported measure is their percentage
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The stimulus duration was calibrated per subject to about 50% detection, so the baseline rate is a design target.
span.note: what this limits: the baseline seen-trial rate reported here: the threshold time was defined as the cue duration producing about 50% of correct stimulus detections within a series of 10 trials, so a baseline near 50% follows from the calibration
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: SHAM rTMS delivered at the same sites, and the effect measured as the difference between real and sham
span.note: eliminates: that the effect is the coil's noise, scalp sensation or the expectation of stimulation rather than the magnetic pulse reaching cortex
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the same sham-difference correlation was computed ACROSS the two experiments as a control comparison
span.note: eliminates: that a correlation between the consciousness and attention measures is a general property of the difference scores rather than a shared mechanism
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: primary consciousness, as measured - THE PERCENTAGE OF `SEEN TRIALS`: the title claims a functional role in primary consciousness and the experiment records how often a subject reported perceiving a cue at their own threshold duration, so a term from consciousness theory and a detection rate occupy the same slot

span.label: the threshold time - EACH SUBJECT'S OWN 50% POINT: defined as the cue duration giving about 50% correct detections over 10 trials, repeated 7 times, so the quantity is fitted per person and every later percentage is measured relative to that fit
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the 52.9% baseline - NEAR THE DESIGN TARGET BY CONSTRUCTION: the calibration sets each subject near 50% detection, so the baseline seen-trial rate is close to the number the procedure aimed at; the rTMS effect is a departure from a value the method placed there, not from a natural rate

span.label: Repetitive TMS over either left or right ventral posterior parietal cortex significantly reduced the number of cue stimuli that subjects consciously reported seeing, compared with sham stimulation.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The same parietal stimulation slowed reaction times to go stimuli relative to sham, indicating an impairment of covert visuospatial attention.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The size of the consciousness impairment and the size of the attention impairment were not correlated across individuals.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Delivering any rTMS, real or sham, speeded reaction times relative to the no-stimulation baseline, so the attentional cost had to be measured against sham rather than baseline.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: A control analysis validated the subjective reports: reaction times were faster on trials the subject called 'seen' than on trials called 'not seen'.
